feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
entry.summary:
Ranking-based Reward Construction (RRC) bridges generative reward models and LLM reinforcement learning by deriving scalar rewards from relative preference rankings instead of absolute scoring paradigms.

Why it matters: RRC enables generative reward models to be effectively utilized as reward functions in reinforcement learning, improving model alignment on chat and reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that unconstrained diffusion LLMs fail at reasoning by committing final answers prematurely before completing chain-of-thought tokens, a pathology resolved using frontier-gated commitment order.

Why it matters: Enforcing sequential token commitment order is required to prevent reasoning collapse in diffusion LLMs without sacrificing their parallel decoding capabilities.

entry.title: BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians
entry.summary:
BaKron accelerates neural network quantization using Kronecker-factored Hessians by combining anti-diagonal parallelism with recursive divide-and-conquer processing.

Why it matters: It enables computationally efficient neural network quantization that leverages rich two-sided curvature information without exceeding the scaling limits of standard GPTQ approaches.

entry.title: The Illusion of Visual Tool-Use: A Causal Audit of Thinking with Images
entry.summary:
A causal audit of multimodal LLM visual tool-use reveals that active visual operations like crop-and-zoom often lack causal effect on final answers despite aggregate accuracy gains.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that visual tool-use in multimodal LLMs frequently incurs high token costs and extra compute without causally driving the model's reasoning or final output.

entry.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
EnvACE is an agentic reinforcement learning method that replaces external environment interactions during training with joint, end-to-end world rehearsal of both tool calls and environment responses.

Why it matters: It removes the need for costly external simulators or real executable environments during LLM agent RL training by internalizing environment dynamics directly into the model.

entry.title: Visual Grounding in Zero-Shot Vision-Language Control
entry.summary:
A systematic input-ablation study of 32,874 VLM controller calls reveals widespread grounding failures in direct zero-shot visual control, while demonstrating that VLMs function reliably as modular hazard assistants when paired with symmetry-consensus guardians.

Why it matters: Current vision-language models are unsuitable as monolithic zero-shot end-to-end controllers, but can safely serve as bounded, selective hazard assistants within modular control architectures.

entry.title: Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
The Globalized Skill Evolution (GSE) framework continuously improves LLM coding agents by co-evolving inter-skill relationships in a graph, consolidating cluster-based skills, and using replay verification to prevent overfitting.

Why it matters: GSE enables LLM software engineering agents to continuously self-improve and generalize across complex tasks without costly full model retraining.

entry.title: Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents
entry.summary:
Contextual Information Policy Optimization (CIPO) is a novel reinforcement learning framework that provides dense, turn-level rewards to align search agent reasoning actions directly with retrieved external evidence without relying on extra reward models.

Why it matters: CIPO improves search agent reliability and efficiency on knowledge-intensive tasks by forcing agents to actively base and revise their multi-step reasoning on retrieved evidence rather than internal guesses.

entry.title: Beyond Sequence Order: Syntax-Informed Positional Embeddings for Transformers
entry.summary:
SiPE introduces syntax-informed positional embeddings that inject a lightweight dependency parse prior into absolute, relative, and rotary Transformers without altering self-attention architecture or degrading perplexity.

Why it matters: It provides a method to incorporate structural language priors into Transformers that enhances downstream task performance and syntactic accuracy while simultaneously improving language model perplexity.

entry.title: When History Lies: Evaluating and Improving Tool Use under Misleading Multi-Turn Histories
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce a paired benchmark and a teacher-student prefix-distillation method to evaluate and mitigate LLM agent tool-calling failures caused by misleading, non-authoritative multi-turn execution histories.

Why it matters: It establishes history reliability as a key bottleneck in multi-turn tool use and provides a scalable distillation approach to prevent agents from using stale or corrupted dialogue context.

entry.title: HERALD: Counterfactual Audits and Minimal Repairs for Proof-of-Retrieval Rewards
entry.summary:
HERALD introduces offline counterfactual audits for search-agent rewards, identifying a citation-laundering vulnerability and proving that a targeted penalty on unretrieved cited passages ($L$) serves as an inclusion-minimal repair.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how counterfactual auditing can detect and fix subtle reward-hacking vulnerabilities in search-agent reward functions without degrading general model performance.

entry.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
AgentOPSD introduces a critic-free, recursive self-distillation method that aggregates token-level log-probability gaps into turn-level credit using Bayesian belief updates in log-odds space for agentic RL.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient way to resolve credit assignment in long-horizon agent tasks without the memory overhead or training instability of a separate critic model.

entry.title: How Far Do Simple Transformations Translate Across Text Embedding Models?
entry.summary:
A study evaluating lightweight linear transformations across nine heterogeneous text embedding models reveals that simple mappings fail to universally translate semantic representations, contradicting the broad latent universality hypothesis.

Why it matters: AI-to-AI latent communication cannot rely solely on simple linear transformations to bridge diverse text embedding spaces without full decoding.

entry.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
entry.summary:
An empirical evaluation of 14 LLMs on BFCL v4 demonstrates that programmatic tool calling using typed Python stubs matches or outperforms native JSON tool calling, with improvements up to 10.6% on the GPT-5.6 family.

Why it matters: Replacing JSON tool calls with programmatic Python scripts offers a more robust, scalable mechanism for agentic tool use without requiring changes to underlying model capabilities.

entry.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
entry.summary:
RP-OPSD improves cross-lingual LLM reasoning transfer by using distributional shifts between teacher views to concentrate on-policy self-distillation on critical reasoning pivots rather than surface text.

Why it matters: It enables more effective cross-lingual reasoning transfer in LLMs by focusing compute and supervision on key decision points rather than language-specific surface text.

entry.title: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
entry.summary:
Evaluation of six observation modes across eight web agent setups shows that task-level representation routing fails to outperform a single fixed mode due to run-to-run noise and sparse supervision signals on weaker agents.

Why it matters: Until web agents achieve higher baseline success rates to generate sufficient training labels, practitioners should default to a single optimal observation mode rather than complex task-level routing pipelines.

entry.title: Causal Episodic Memory for Feedback-Driven Agent Repair
entry.summary:
MERIT is a training-free LLM agent that improves Text-to-SQL error repair by maintaining an online dual-polarity memory of oracle-verified corrections and failed attempts from past episodes.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that agents can incrementally improve code and SQL generation performance across successive query tasks using lightweight, episodic memory without costly parameter updates.

entry.title: Decomposed Entailment for Factuality Checking and Hallucination Detection
entry.summary:
HallDetect is a lightweight, black-box hallucination detection framework that decomposes text into atomic claims and evaluates them against multi-scale source chunks using a compact encoder-based entailment model and asymmetric score aggregation.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, resource-efficient, and interpretable hallucination detection across diverse source-grounded generation tasks on consumer-grade hardware.

entry.title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify an irreversible skill-contamination phase transition in self-evolving LLM agents and introduce Verifier-as-Gatekeeper (VaG), a pre-commit gating framework that prevents defective skills from entering the decision context.

Why it matters: Preventing defective skills prior to integration is essential for LLM agents, as post-hoc skill deletion fails to reverse reasoning flaws inherited by downstream distilled skills.

entry.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning
entry.summary:
On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD2) uses the probability gap between a post-trained teacher and its base model to outperform standard On-Policy Distillation in multilingual math reasoning across English, Korean, and Japanese.

Why it matters: It provides a more effective post-training distillation method that strengthens non-English mathematical reasoning without causing output language drift.

entry.title: Task-Conditional Flow Matching for Balanced Multilingual Text Embedding Adaptation
entry.summary:
Task-Conditional Flow Matching (TCFM) selectively applies Flow Matching to translation tasks while using task-aligned objectives for retrieval, classification, and pair-classification to improve multilingual embedding adaptation.

Why it matters: TCFM demonstrates that tailoring training objectives to specific task dynamics rather than using a single uniform objective significantly improves multilingual text embedding quality and generalization.

entry.title: GROM: Gradient-Free Rapid One-Shot Machine Unlearning
entry.summary:
GROM introduces a gradient-free, one-shot machine unlearning method that uses a ridge-regularized least-squares closed-form analytical update to permanently remove targeted LLM knowledge in seconds.

Why it matters: It provides an orders-of-magnitude faster unlearning process that securely erases sensitive LLM data without susceptibility to quantization-based knowledge recovery attacks.

entry.title: Once a Response, Always a Response: Detecting LLM-generated Text via Latent Prompt Restoration
entry.summary:
EchoPrompt is a training-free, zero-shot LLM-generated text detector that quantifies latent prompt dependency by measuring likelihood gain from a generic assistant-response context restored via an instruction-tuned model and calibrated against a base model.

Why it matters: By explicitly modeling the instruction-following generation mechanism rather than relying solely on statistical probability discrepancies, EchoPrompt improves zero-shot detection robustness against AI-generated text risks.

entry.title: Mitigating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge via Random Number Generation
entry.summary:
A novel method mitigates LLM-as-a-Judge scoring bias by measuring an LLM's task-specific latent number bias via random number generation and rectifying token generation probabilities accordingly.

Why it matters: It provides a task-specific calibration technique to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-based automated evaluation systems without requiring reference texts.

entry.title: Reasoning Errors Have a Region and a Direction in the Residual-Stream Trajectory of LLMs
entry.summary:
A novel three-stream detector evaluates LLM reasoning accuracy by combining residual-stream motion (displacements) with state context (coarse region via vector quantization and fine direction via normalized multi-layer states) rather than relying on static states or decontextualized trajectories alone.

Why it matters: It enables more reliable identification of LLM reasoning errors and factual hallucinations across diverse tasks without requiring full-state probing or task-specific retraining.

entry.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks
entry.summary:
Recursive Synthetic Terminal Tasks (RST) is a verified synthesis framework that recursively extends, realigns, and validates terminal tasks, producing 37,484 long-horizon agent tasks at approximately $0.05 per task.

Why it matters: RST provides a scalable, low-cost method to synthesize increasingly complex, verified training data for terminal agents, significantly boosting their performance on long-horizon benchmarks.

entry.title: AgentOPSD: Recursive Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
AgentOPSD is a critic-free agentic RL method that converts sparse outcome rewards into turn-level credit signals using recursive Bayesian belief updates on teacher-student log-probability gaps.

Why it matters: It provides dense, turn-level credit assignment for complex multi-turn agent tasks without the computational overhead of training a separate critic network or generating extra rollout trajectories.

entry.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale
entry.summary:
WorldClaw is a coarse-to-fine, agentic framework that generates large-scale, editable 3D open worlds from text prompts by combining LLM planning agents with terrain conditioning and render-based refinement agents.

Why it matters: It enables the automated generation of massive, spatially coherent 3D environments with fully editable, instance-level assets suitable for downstream editing and interactive applications.

entry.title: EnvACE: Internalizing Environment Dynamics via World Rehearsal for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
EnvACE replaces external environment interactions during LLM agent RL training with end-to-end joint optimization of action generation and environment response rehearsal.

Why it matters: EnvACE enables effective agentic RL scaling without the cost, verification bottlenecks, or grounding issues associated with building real or external environment simulators.

entry.title: Learning from Failures: Retrieval-Centric CoT via Hard Negatives for Unified Multimodal Retrieval
entry.summary:
UniME-R1 is an embedder-adviser framework that uses hard negatives to generate Retrieval-Centric Chain-of-Thought (RC-CoT) reasoning based on initial retrieval feedback rather than query-only context.

Why it matters: Conditioning reasoning on actual retrieval failures allows Large Vision-Language Models to refine queries and resolve fine-grained ambiguities that direct encoding misses.

entry.title: ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction
entry.summary:
ChronoVision is a multimodal framework that enhances multi-step temporal reasoning by reconstructing latent image states and applying reinforcement learning with implicit process grounding and visual attention targeting.

Why it matters: It mitigates the ambiguity of language-only reasoning in MLLMs by grounding temporal visual transformations directly in the visual latent space.

entry.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation for Multilingual Math Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD^2) for multilingual math reasoning using Qwen3 across English, Korean, and Japanese.

Why it matters: OPD^2 offers an effective alternative to reinforcement learning for multilingual post-training, but requires target-language data to prevent model outputs from drifting into English.

entry.title: GST-Bench: Can VLMs Develop Global Spatial Awareness from Video?
entry.summary:
GST-Bench evaluates global spatial intelligence in vision-language models using synthetic videos, exposing a massive performance gap between state-of-the-art models (42.68%) and humans (79.08%).

Why it matters: Current VLMs lack the global scene representation capabilities required for embodied agents to navigate and reason accurately across long-horizon continuous video.

entry.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
entry.summary:
HarnessOpt-Bench is a new benchmark that evaluates LLMs on their ability to iteratively optimize agent harnesses (prompts, tools, and control flow) under stochastic, budget-constrained evaluation conditions.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized, discriminative protocol to measure and improve how effectively AI models can autonomously optimize the software environments of other agentic systems.

entry.title: K-EXAONE 2.0 Technical Report
entry.summary:
LG AI Research released K-EXAONE 2.0, an open-weight, Apache 2.0-licensed Mixture-of-Experts foundation model upcycled from K-EXAONE, featuring 750B total parameters, 37B active parameters, and a 256K token context window.

Why it matters: Its open-source Apache 2.0 license and low active-parameter ratio enable cost-effective deployment and research on high-capacity, long-context multilingual tasks.

entry.title: DyPES-VLA: Learning Shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific Control for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
entry.summary:
DyPES-VLA is a cross-embodiment Vision-Language-Action model that pairs shared dynamics priors trained via future-prediction objectives with an embodiment-specific Mixture-of-Experts action head operating directly in native action spaces.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for manual action space preprocessing, allowing a single generalist model to control diverse robot architectures using native control semantics.

entry.title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
World-to-Wrist VLA introduces task-conditioned future wrist latent modeling and a structured annotation pipeline to improve fine-grained, contact-sensitive robot manipulation while maintaining over 80 Hz action-generation rates.

Why it matters: It improves the execution of precise, contact-heavy robotic tasks by explicitly predicting local wrist perspective changes within global task constraints without sacrificing real-time control speed.

entry.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
entry.summary:
CalibForge is an autonomous task synthesis system that uses multi-solver and contrastive adversarial calibration to revise executable terminal tasks into a solver-relative learnable zone for agent training.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that calibrating synthesized tasks to solver ability creates more effective and transferable supervision data for training terminal execution agents.

entry.title: WorldCycle: Self-Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Video World Models
entry.summary:
WorldCycle is a self-verifiable reinforcement learning framework that uses reversible action cycles to provide annotation-free supervision, reducing long-horizon video world model compounding errors without requiring ground-truth future states.

Why it matters: It solves the verification bottleneck in post-training video world models, enabling more accurate, physically grounded long-horizon planning and exploration without manual annotations.

entry.title: SmartMage: Dynamic Modality Orchestration for 3D Scene Understanding
entry.summary:
SmartMage is a unified Multimodal Large Language Model that dynamically selects and routes heterogeneous visual and geometric modalities for 3D scene understanding based on query needs.

Why it matters: It eliminates the computational waste and semantic noise caused by fixed modality combinations, enabling more efficient and accurate 3D reasoning in embodied AI systems.

entry.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the MIST benchmark, the SC2W susceptibility metric, and SCOPE, a DPO-based method that trains language models to selectively trust external context without blindly ignoring valid inputs.

Why it matters: It prevents language models from either blindly following deceptive context or becoming unhelpful by ignoring external context entirely.

entry.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models by using adaptive propagation gates to dynamically weight token-level supervision based on how local teacher-student divergences evolve across time.

Why it matters: DASH increases the efficiency and accuracy of Dense RLVR self-distillation without introducing any additional computational overhead from extra forward passes.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
entry.summary:
Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation (U-OPSD) enables LLMs to self-correct without external supervision by distilling pseudo-solutions derived from self-consistency into prefixes of their longest incorrect completions.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that LLM post-training and self-correction can match or exceed supervised baseline performance without relying on ground-truth labels, environmental feedback, or larger teacher models.

entry.title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers
entry.summary:
MACRO enables parameter-free dynamic layer routing in LLMs by modeling layer execution paths as a context-dependent Markov policy decoded with a top-k Viterbi algorithm.

Why it matters: MACRO provides a faster, parameter-free way to optimize dynamic inference paths in open-weight LLMs without retraining weights or adding heavy search latency.

entry.title: Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models
entry.summary:
Hierarchical Latent Prediction (HiLP) introduces an auxiliary higher-level abstract latent to standard language model pre-training, mitigating compounding rollout errors in latent-space predictions.

Why it matters: HiLP enables language models to reason and plan over longer horizons while improving inference speed through more efficient speculative decoding.

entry.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
entry.summary:
AV-AIVAT combines Action-Informed Value Assessment Tool variance reduction with continuously monitored Confidence Sequences to enable certified, anytime-valid early stopping in imperfect-information game evaluations.

Why it matters: It drastically cuts computation, model inference, and execution costs during agent evaluation by allowing evaluations to stop safely the exact moment statistical evidence is sufficient.

entry.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
entry.summary:
A new trace-grounded parametric profiling method reveals that Video Language Models fail at simple event counting, exhibiting a staged temporal failure driven by event representation, count, and frequency.

Why it matters: Aggregate accuracy metrics can mask severe temporal reasoning failures in video language models, as increased frame sampling may artificially inflate final scores without recovering actual event sequences.

entry.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
entry.summary:
TrajDebug is a framework that identifies critical failures in long-horizon LLM agent trajectories using multi-granularity history compression, evidence-based error detection, and error-lifecycle tracing to measure terminal impact.

Why it matters: TrajDebug allows developers to pinpoint the root cause of cascading failures in complex LLM agent trajectories, providing actionable diagnoses to increase downstream task completion rates.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced a reference-free framework that utilizes LLM judges to evaluate conversational-agent benchmarks based on consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized, automated way to diagnose and improve the quality of conversational agent benchmarks, ensuring more reliable performance evaluations.

entry.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
entry.summary:
HarnessOpt-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs on end-to-end, evaluation-guided harness optimization under strict budget and resource constraints.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, discriminative framework to measure and improve an LLM's ability to automatically engineer and optimize agentic control systems.

entry.title: ToolArtist: Tool-Using Unified Multimodal Models for Agentic Image Generation
entry.summary:
ToolArtist is a fully agentic image generation framework that post-trains a Unified Multimodal Model to dynamically coordinate reasoning, external tool usage, and native image generation under a single unified policy.

Why it matters: Unifying multi-step reasoning, external search tools, and image synthesis into a single policy significantly improves complex open-world text-to-image generation tasks.

entry.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment
entry.summary:
ABSeeker introduces Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment (ABC), a framework that converts sparse trajectory-level outcomes into dense, step-level supervision for training long-horizon search agents via SFT and RL.

Why it matters: Dense step-level credit assignment allows small 4B-parameter models to match the search performance of 30B-scale agents while utilizing low data volumes.

entry.title: The Personalization Mirage: How LLMs Fabricate User Profiles, and Why Self-Monitoring Misleads
entry.summary:
A new benchmark, MirageBench, reveals that LLMs fabricate unsupported user attributes 35%–49% of the time, and that cross-model self-reported confidence negatively correlates with actual measured faithfulness.

Why it matters: Developers cannot rely on an LLM's self-reported confidence to select reliable personalization models, making external verification essential for persistent memory systems.

entry.title: Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes
entry.summary:
A systematic empirical study analyzes multimodal pretraining mechanics, establishing that early joint modality training avoids 'vision laziness' and identifying architectural designs that enable high-performance visual generation using 5% of standard compute budgets.

Why it matters: It offers actionable architectural principles and recipes to drastically reduce the compute budget required for training unified multimodal models while avoiding language-prior reliance.

entry.title: OneDayAgent: Towards a Long-Horizon Harness for Autonomous Agents
entry.summary:
OneDayAgent is a long-horizon agent harness that decomposes tasks, manages memory under context limits, and verifies outputs, setting an 0.821 state-of-the-art score on AgentIF-OneDay.

Why it matters: It provides a unified, cross-model framework to jointly mitigate goal drift, state loss, and context overflow in complex long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
entry.summary:
GDPevo is an evolution-native benchmark for evaluating AI agent self-evolution across enterprise workflows using a rule hybridization pipeline that generates training and held-out test tasks.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized, contamination-resistant benchmark to reliably measure how well autonomous agents learn from experience and transfer knowledge to real-world business workflows.

entry.title: When Teachers Mislead: Spurious-Signal-Aware On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SA-OPD introduces a spurious-signal-aware on-policy distillation framework that filters misleading token-level teacher signals by evaluating both input-groundedness and optimization impact across LLMs and VLMs.

Why it matters: It prevents student models from absorbing misleading, input-agnostic teacher biases, leading to more precise and efficient on-policy model distillation.

entry.title: Toward Skill-Native LLMs: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Long-Horizon Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Skill Entropy to measure skill-switching difficulty in LLMs, evaluated models via the Skill^2-Bench benchmark, and proposed Skill-Entropy RL to improve long-horizon multi-skill reasoning performance.

Why it matters: Incorporating skill entropy into reinforcement learning enables language models to better execute complex, multi-step tasks that require dynamic transitions between diverse reasoning skills.

entry.title: NOLLI: A Difficulty-Calibrated Puzzle Benchmark for Diagnosing the English-Korean Performance Gap
entry.summary:
NOLLI is a procedurally generated, difficulty-calibrated puzzle benchmark comprising 15 puzzle types (7,500 items) designed to isolate and diagnose the causes of English-Korean model performance gaps.

Why it matters: The benchmark reveals that English-Korean performance gaps stem from complex sub-syllabic manipulation and specific cultural reasoning deficits rather than simple language translation overhead.

entry.title: Decoding Children's Gait Behavior
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced a dataset of over 1,100 60-FPS RGB videos and pose sequences to benchmark fine-grained pediatric gait analysis for clinical diagnosis, revealing that existing gait models and MLLMs fail to capture these nuances.

Why it matters: It enables non-intrusive, low-cost screening and clinical assessment for pediatric developmental and neuromuscular disorders like cerebral palsy using standard RGB video instead of expensive 3D sensor systems.

entry.title: When Memory Lies: An Empirical Study of Spatial Memory Staleness in VLM Agents
entry.summary:
A study using a dynamic FrozenLake testbed evaluates VLM memory staleness, revealing that unverified spatial memory doubles agent mortality compared to no memory and that text-based solvability fails to translate to reliable visual grounding.

Why it matters: Deploying memory-augmented VLM agents in dynamic environments without reliable visual auditing creates severe safety risks, as stale memory actively degrades performance compared to zero-memory baselines.

entry.title: RestoreKV: Recovering Full-Cache Behavior Under Aggressive Query-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction
entry.summary:
RestoreKV restores full-cache performance during query-agnostic KV cache eviction by using LoRA-adapted restore tokens to generate a compact complement cache during prefill without altering the base importance scorer.

Why it matters: RestoreKV recovers lost accuracy under extreme KV cache compression budgets without requiring task-specific fine-tuning or adding query-time decoding overhead.

entry.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance
entry.summary:
RSTG enhances GRPO post-training by adaptively applying on-policy teacher distillation to negative zero-variance prompts and high-entropy/high-divergence tokens, combined with SFT on teacher-generated correct trajectories.

Why it matters: It resolves gradient sparsity and exploratory degradation in GRPO by extracting dense, selective learning signals from teacher models when student reinforcement learning fails.

entry.title: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
entry.summary:
FocusMem factorizes latent memory for GUI agents into role-aware content, state-conditioned readout, and a trust gate, improving retrieval and decision-making while keeping the underlying GUI policy frozen.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that decoupling memory content, readout, and trust allows latent memory interfaces to scale context and filter noise without requiring expensive retraining of the underlying policy model.

entry.title: HelloWorld: Enabling Socially Interactive Characters in Video World Models
entry.summary:
HelloWorld introduces a video world model enabling real-time, user-triggered social interactions with on-screen characters via self-distillation and temporal cross-attention mask modulation.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between passive video world generation and dynamic, camera-directed character interactions without compromising aesthetic quality or camera-pose control.

entry.title: Protoreasoning in Tiny Transformers
entry.summary:
Tiny ~1M-parameter transformers using protoreasoning—a simplified Chain of Thought on Dyck languages—demonstrate that token trace content, rather than extra computation tokens, significantly closes the out-of-distribution generalization gap.

Why it matters: It enables cheap, fine-grained mechanistic analysis of algorithmic generalization and step-by-step reasoning on highly accessible ~1M-parameter models without requiring opaque, compute-intensive frontier LLMs.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning
entry.summary:
ReCo is a step-wise framework using a process-reward estimator to dynamically coordinate KV-cache compression, penalize reflection tokens, and trigger early stopping based on trajectory confidence.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers inference cost and latency for Large Reasoning Models by jointly optimizing cache size and generation length using process rewards.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Can Be Unreliable in Implicit-Influence Settings
entry.summary:
A new benchmark reveals that Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring detection rates drop by up to 46 percentage points under implicit-influence settings compared to explicit-influence settings across seven frontier extended-thinking models.

Why it matters: Evaluating CoT monitors solely under explicit concealment instructions overestimates their reliability, as implicit biases can covertly manipulate model behavior without triggering safety monitors.

entry.title: Toward Skill-Native LLMs: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Long-Horizon Reasoning
entry.summary:
This paper introduces Skill Entropy to measure cross-skill switching difficulty in long-horizon tasks, introducing the Skill^2-Bench benchmark and a Skill-Entropy RL training framework that improves multi-skill reasoning performance.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to better navigate complex, multi-step tasks by providing a concrete method and training signal for transitioning smoothly between different domain skills.

entry.title: Leak-Resistant Unlearning: A New Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Consistency and Recovery Robustness
entry.summary:
A new benchmark evaluates LLM machine unlearning against complex multi-hop reasoning paths and post-unlearning recovery attacks across three models and six unlearning methods.

Why it matters: Static unlearning evaluations are insufficient, as unlearned knowledge can still be extracted through indirect reasoning paths or restored via post-unlearning adaptation.

entry.title: K-EXAONE 2.0 Technical Report
entry.summary:
LG AI Research released K-EXAONE 2.0, an open-weight, upcycled 750B Mixture-of-Experts multilingual model activating 37B parameters per token with a 256K context length under an Apache 2.0 license.

Why it matters: The open-weight Apache 2.0 release provides the AI community with a frontier-scale MoE model optimized for long-context understanding, agentic coding, and localized Korean safety requirements.

entry.title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning
entry.summary:
Argus is a general-purpose, fixed-weight agentic runtime featuring role-based orchestration (Manager, Planner, Engineer, Reviewer) and task-native verification to achieve self-evolution across long-horizon software engineering, mathematics, and ML engineering tasks.

Why it matters: Argus demonstrates that persistent, role-structured runtimes can autonomously self-evolve, recover from failures, and solve long-horizon tasks without updating underlying model weights.

entry.title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling
entry.summary:
OctoLong introduces a context engineering pipeline that creates dependency-rich, multi-million-token cross-repository code contexts for long-context language model mid-training.

Why it matters: Incorporating structured cross-repository code dependencies during mid-training significantly enhances a model's long-context reasoning and repository-level code understanding without relying solely on limited traditional text corpora.

entry.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
entry.summary:
OPD-V is a visual on-policy self-distillation paradigm that uses Positive and Negative Teachers to enforce Modality Balance, improving MLLM reasoning performance while lowering training costs.

Why it matters: It enables more effective multimodal post-training by ensuring MLLMs properly incorporate visual context rather than relying excessively on text generation.

entry.title: Chained Recursive Language Models for Multi-Iteration Reasoning
entry.summary:
Chained RLM is an inference-time architecture that repeatedly calls an LLM as fresh reasoning roots using plain-text summaries, blackboards, and durable artifacts instead of inheriting full conversational history.

Why it matters: It improves reasoning accuracy on complex multi-hop tasks by preventing context clutter and early error propagation through structured, artifact-based context management.

entry.title: JoyAI-Video-Edit: Real-Time Open-Ended Video Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion
entry.summary:
JoyAI-Video-Edit is a 16B-parameter autoregressive diffusion framework that enables real-time, open-ended 720p video editing at 30 FPS on a single Nvidia B200 GPU without future frame access.

Why it matters: It proves that open-ended, streaming video editing can achieve real-time 30 FPS performance while maintaining temporal consistency and matching offline editor quality.

entry.title: MerchantBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Long-Term Coherence in E-Commerce Operations
entry.summary:
MerchantBench is a 365-day e-commerce simulation benchmark using 98,843 real product records and 26 tools to test LLM agents' long-term coherence across extended operational horizons.

Why it matters: The benchmark exposes a severe performance gap in current LLMs when forced to maintain coherent, multi-step decisions over long timeframes with delayed real-world feedback.

entry.title: InfiniSplat: Implicit Gaussian Decoding for Large-Baseline Monocular View Synthesis
entry.summary:
InfiniSplat introduces a feed-forward single-image 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that uses geometry-guided sampling and an implicit decoder to replace pixel-aligned primitives with surface-aligned representations for large-baseline view synthesis.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, structurally coherent novel view synthesis from a single image across large viewpoint shifts without requiring per-scene optimization or multi-view capture.

entry.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
entry.summary:
AURORA-LM introduces a continuous-latent diffusion language model combining a Query-based Encoder-Decoder for prefix-aligned text latents with a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer using flow matching.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that continuous-latent diffusion models can achieve superior text generation and summarization performance without sacrificing token-level decoder capacity.

entry.title: Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0: A Unified Multimodal Model for Scalable 3D Generation, Understanding, and Editing
entry.summary:
Hunyuan3D-Buffalo 1.0 is a unified 3D multimodal framework that integrates 3D understanding, text-to-3D generation, instruction-guided editing, and text-grounded part generation within a single architecture.

Why it matters: It proves that unified multimodal pre-training across understanding and generation solves data scarcity in 3D editing and improves overall geometric consistency.

entry.title: Knowledge-Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation
entry.summary:
KGD decouples pretrained behavioral knowledge from task-specific geometry using Behavioral Multi-Token Prediction and Anchored Calibration Residuals, enabling continuous model refreshing without task-gradient interference in streaming recommendation.

Why it matters: It solves parameter conflict during continual pretrain-transfer refreshes, allowing industrial recommendation systems to update behavioral models in production without disrupting task-specific adaptations.

entry.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
PCSD improves agentic reinforcement learning by deriving continuous token-level self-distillation weights from the local persistence of teacher-favoring signals using adaptive windows, exponential decay, and trend-aware modulation.

Why it matters: PCSD provides robust, dense token-level supervision in multi-turn RL environments, mitigating teacher noise and improving agent generalization on unseen tasks.

entry.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
entry.summary:
This paper introduces Agent-Centric Interactive World Proxies, shifting world modeling from raw physical-state prediction to agent-usable information transitions like execution outcomes, memory retrieval, and verification signals.

Why it matters: It expands world modeling beyond physical simulation, offering a structured framework to safely and efficiently train and guide AI agents using controllable, low-cost feedback.

entry.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
entry.summary:
PAST-Bench benchmarks recursive self-improvement in personal AI agents across controlled task sequences, evaluating performance gains from retained experience against Hermes+, an agent framework with five targeted interventions across the agent loop.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized diagnostic framework to measure whether and how persistent personal agents convert historical session experience into genuine, pathway-verified self-improvement.

entry.title: To Add Is Machine, To Delete Is Human: Measuring and Mitigating Deletion Avoidance in LLM Code Editing
entry.summary:
Researchers identify deletion avoidance in LLMs, showing models fail to remove unnecessary code, and demonstrate that post-training targeting deletion reduces this behavior and improves overall code editing.

Why it matters: LLM code editors generate test-passing patches that systematically bloat codebases and increase technical debt by retaining code meant for removal.

entry.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
entry.summary:
Video-DeepResearch extends multimodal agents to continuous video via a decoupled perception-exploration pipeline, stage-wise tool unlocking, and GRPO reinforcement learning, outperforming proprietary models on complex video reasoning.

Why it matters: The framework demonstrates that open-weights models trained with stage-wise tool policies and RL can outperform leading proprietary LLMs on complex, multi-hop video research tasks.

entry.title: Any-OPD: Heterogeneous On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Matching Models via Representation-Space Bridging
entry.summary:
Any-OPD enables on-policy distillation between heterogeneous latent flow-matching models by comparing decoded outputs within a frozen, model-agnostic vision representation space rather than relying on matching architectures, VAE latents, or timestep grids.

Why it matters: It allows developers to distill state-of-the-art generative capabilities from large, proprietary-style teacher models into much smaller deployment models even when their latent spaces, VAEs, and architectures are completely incompatible.

entry.title: OmniPack: Unified Token Compression for Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Models
entry.summary:
OmniPack is a training-free framework that combines pre-LLM structural token compression with inner-LLM query-conditioned semantic refinement to optimize efficiency in omni-modal large language models.

Why it matters: It enables drastically reduced computational overhead for audio-visual LLM inference without requiring retrained models or sacrificing significant task performance.

entry.title: UniWorld-Design: From Pixel Generation to Layer-Native Design
entry.summary:
UniWorld-Design introduces a layer-native framework featuring Text-to-RGBA and Image-to-Layer models that generate, decompose, and edit images as complete semantic RGBA layers rather than flat pixel grids.

Why it matters: By treating complete RGBA layers as atomic units, generative models enable realistic, flexible image editing where individual elements can be moved or removed without leaving pixel artifacts.

entry.title: CAPEval: A Decoupled Caption Evaluation across Understanding and Generation
entry.summary:
CAPEval decouples caption quality into Coverage and Precision, revealing that Coverage correlates with downstream multimodal understanding performance while Precision predicts text-to-image generation performance.

Why it matters: Decoupling caption metrics allows researchers to select and optimize captioners specifically tailored for either multimodal understanding or text-to-image generation tasks.

entry.title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
entry.summary:
TurnSight is a turn-level hindsight self-distillation framework for tool-integrated reasoning that derives dense supervision from execution-conditioned hindsight and cross-horizon agreement to adaptively modulate RL advantages.

Why it matters: It improves reinforcement learning for long-horizon tool-integrated LLMs by offering fine-grained, state-grounded credit assignment without relying on external privileged context.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
entry.summary:
This paper establishes a unified three-axis framework for test-time scaling in LLMs, standardizing inference regimes, evaluation profiles, and reproducibility requirements while releasing over 2 billion full reasoning traces.

Why it matters: It establishes standardized accounting for compute, protocols, and evaluation, enabling rigorous, reproducible comparisons across disparate inference-time search and sampling strategies.

entry.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
entry.summary:
ReflectRL is a lightweight plug-and-play framework that uses failed expert trajectories (Golden Negative Trajectories) during on-policy training to elicit reflective reasoning and transfer it back to direct reasoning.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to convert previously wasted expert failure data into effective training signals without requiring successful reference trajectories.

entry.title: Interpretable Adaptive Sampling for LLM Test-Time Scaling
entry.summary:
A lightweight fuzzy controller dynamically assigns LLM test-time sampling budgets per query based on prompt complexity and model confidence, reducing average samples while maintaining reasoning performance.

Why it matters: It enables more compute-efficient LLM inference by providing inspectable, query-specific sample allocation without sacrificing output accuracy.

entry.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
entry.summary:
Logic pre-pretraining (Logic-PPT) initializes language models on formal derivations, accelerating natural language skill acquisition and improving model compressibility at scale.

Why it matters: Using formal logic as a pre-training phase significantly reduces the token budget required to achieve target task accuracy and yields smaller, highly compressible models.

entry.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
entry.summary:
Researchers identify a fundamental alignment tension between reasoning faithfulness and safety in Large Reasoning Models, introducing the HazMart benchmark and a Targeted Reasoning Replacement technique to measure and steer these behavior trade-offs.

Why it matters: Understanding and resolving the tension between faithfulness and safety is critical for building trustworthy, monitorable AI systems that predictably reject unsafe actions.

entry.title: Muon Meets Mamba: Spectral Optimization for State Space Models
entry.summary:
Applying the Muon optimizer specifically to the output projection of Mamba-2 130M improves token efficiency over AdamW, whereas applying it to input projections or both projections yields worse results.

Why it matters: Selective application of spectral optimizers like Muon to specific layers enables token-efficiency gains in non-Transformer architectures like State Space Models.

entry.title: Sparse Weight Decomposition for Efficient Circuit Extraction
entry.summary:
Sparse Weight Decomposition (SWD) reparameterizes pretrained linear transformer weight matrices into two sparse factors, creating addressable circuit units for extraction without training auxiliary sparse models or incurring high computational costs.

Why it matters: SWD significantly reduces the computational burden and data requirements for mechanistically interpreting LLMs without sacrificing fidelity or introducing a gap between analyzed features and original weights.

entry.title: Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer in LLM Families: A Closed-Form Linear Mapping for Prefill Reuse
entry.summary:
A closed-form ridge regression mapper enables cross-model KV cache transfer between different-sized LLM family members, bypassing prefill computation by mapping source KV pairs to target layers.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute latency and cost when dynamically routing or swapping context between different-sized models within the same family.

entry.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
Omega-S is a data-free, weight-only penalty that reduces catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning by regularizing node degree variance, adding under 4% step overhead without requiring old data or Fisher matrices.

Why it matters: Omega-S offers an easily implemented three-line training loss addition that significantly preserves base model capabilities during targeted fine-tuning without the memory and data overhead of traditional regularization methods.
